{{nihongo|'''Inatsuhiko Shrine'''|為那都比古神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Settsu Province]].

=== Enshrined God ===
The following eight deities are enshrined. </ref>.
; Main enshrined deity
:* Tamenatsuhiko Okami
:* Tamenatsuhime Okami
; jointly enshrined deity
:* {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Omikami}}, {{ill|Oyamakui no Kami|Q10935105|qid=Q10935105}}, {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|Q1781862|qid=Q1781862|lt=Konohanasakuyahimekami}}
:: {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|Q2564508|qid=Q2564508|lt=Amagoyane Mikoto}}, {{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|Q1640658|qid=Q1640658|lt=Hinokagu Earth God}}, {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|ar|سوغاوارا نو ميتشيزانه|br|Sugawara no Michizane|ckb|سوگاوارا نۆ میچیزانێ|de|Sugawara no Michizane|es|Sugawara no Michizane|fa|سوگاوارا نو میچی‌زانه|fi|Sugawara no Michizane|fr|Sugawara no Michizane|id|Sugawara no Michizane|it|Sugawara no Michizane|ja|菅原道真|kk|Сугавара но Митидзане|ko|스가와라노 미치자네|la|Sugawara no Michizane|ms|Sugawara no Michizane|nl|Sugawara no Michizane|nn|Sugawara no Michizane|pl|Michizane Sugawara|pt|Sugawara no Michizane|ru|Сугавара-но Митидзанэ|sh|Sugawara no Michizane|sv|Sugawara no Michizane|th|สึกาวาระ โนะ มิจิซาเนะ|tr|Sugawara no Michizane|uk|Суґавара но Мітідзане|zh|菅原道真|zh_classical|菅原道真|zh_min_nan|Sugawara no Mitizane|qid=Q382005}}
{{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Extended}} "{{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448}}" established in 5 years ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}) {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=In the Shinto Name Book}}, there is a mention of ``Tamenatuhiko Shrine 2,'' and these 2 shrines can be compared to the two gods Tamenatuhiko-kami and Tamenatuhime-kami {{Sfn|Tamenatsuhiko Shrine (Gods)|2000}}. However, Tamenatsuhime is a deity enshrined at the former Omiya Shrine (currently closed; the site is Hakushima, Minoh City), and was enshrined in our company in {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}}40 ({{ill|1907|Q2048|qid=Q2048}}).{{Sfn|Tamenatsuhiko Shrine (Gods)|2000}}. Other shrines including Amaterasu Omikami were also enshrined together in 1901.<ref name="Explanation board"/>

=== About the enshrined deity ===
[[File:Daigu-ji (Mino), hondou.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Iouzan Daiguji (Hakushima, Minoh City)}}]]
The ``Ina'' in the names of the two main deities (Tamenatsuhikokami and Tamenatsuhimekami) are derived from place names. In addition to "Tamena", it is also written as "Ina", "Tamena", "Tamena", etc. {{Sfn|Tamenatsuhiko Shrine (Gods)|2000}}, {{ill|Ina River|arz|نهر اينا (نهر فى اليابان)|ja|猪名川|ru|Инагава (река, Осака)|qid=Q11571867}} basin ({{ill|Settsu Province|ca|Província de Settsu|cs|Provincie Seccu|de|Provinz Settsu|eo|Provinco Seccu|es|Provincia de Settsu|fa|ولایت ستسو|fr|Province de Settsu|gl|Provincia de Settsu|hak|Settsu-koet|id|Provinsi Settsu|it|Settsu (provincia)|ja|摂津国|ko|셋쓰국|lt|Seccu žemė|nl|Settsu (provincie)|pt|Província de Settsu|ru|Сэтцу (провинция)|simple|Settsu Province|sk|Seccu (provincia)|sr|Провинција Сецу|tr|Settsu (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Сеццу|zh|攝津國|zh_min_nan|Settu-kok|zh_yue|攝津國|qid=Q864163}}{{ill|Teshima district|Q11633558|qid=Q11633558|lt=Toshima County}}/{{ill|Kawabe District, Hyōgo|ceb|Kawanabe-gun|es|Distrito de Kawabe|fr|District de Kawabe|id|Distrik Kawabe, Hyōgo|it|Distretto di Kawabe|ja|川辺郡|ko|가와베군|pl|Powiat Kawabe|ru|Кавабе (уезд, Хёго)|zh|川邊郡|qid=Q1042053|lt=Kawabe County}}) It was the name of a wide area. Place names like this There are many known examples of gods and people with the name Hiko/Hime, such as {{ill|Kibitsuhiko-no-mikoto|Q65318|qid=Q65318|lt=Kibitsuhiko}} and {{ill|Isetsuhiko|Q17193127|qid=Q17193127}}, and the case of ``Tamenatsuhiko/Hime'' is the same. It is assumed that this was the deification of the chieftains of powerful clans in the Ina region. However, there are various opinions as to which clan it is specifically compared to (see {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Review section}}).Also, as mentioned above, Tamenatsuhime is the enshrined deity of Omiya Shrine in Hakushima, Minoh City {{Sfn|Tamenatsuhiko Shrine (Gods)|2000}}. The two gods of Tamenatsuhiko and Tamenatsuhime lived for {{ill|Kanpyō (era)|Q1346292|qid=Q1346292}} years ({{ill|889|Q23833|qid=Q23833}}-{{ja link|898|Q24131}}), it is said to have been divided into separate shrines. is written in the Katsuo-ji Temple document of {{ill|Shōka (era)|Q1327489|qid=Q1327489}} 3rd year ({{ill|1259|Q5507|qid=Q5507}}), which states, The description of ``Tenma Tenjin'' is recognized. This Omiya Shrine was abolished after being enshrined in 1901, and only the Yakushi-do Hall remains of the former {{ill|Jingū-ji|Q1074971|qid=Q1074971}} {{Sfn|Tamenatsuhiko Shrine (Gods)|2000}}. Near the site, there is a huge rock (Yoga Rock/Io Rock) that is said to have been visited by a god, and in addition, in "{{ill|Setyo Gundan|Q11498591|qid=Q11498591}}" and "Settsu Shi" Since only the explanation of Omiya Shrine is included in the section on Tamenatsuhiko Shrine, there is also a theory that Omiya Shrine is the main shrine of the Shikinai shrine ``Tamenatuhiko Shrine Niza'' {{Sfn|Tamenatsuhiko Shrine (Gods)|2000}}.Furthermore, at one time, the deity enshrined at Tamenatsuhiko Shrine was {{ill|Gozu Tennō|Q11570247|qid=Q11570247}}, and the shrine itself was also called ``Tenno'' {{Sfn|Tamenatuhiko Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}. Regarding this, in "{{ill|Settsu Meisho Zue|ja|摂津名所図会|qid=Q11498549}}", it is said that in the {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} years ({{ill|1573|Q6678|qid=Q6678}}-{{ill|1592|Q6769|qid=Q6769}}), When Nobunaga|Q171411}} had {{ill|Justo Takayama|Q749873|qid=Q749873}} rename the temples and shrines of Settsu Province, our Shinjin complained that the name of the god was changed to Gozu Tenno (Nobunaga's guardian deity), so he was spared the trouble.{{Sfn|Tamenatsuhiko Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}.

{{ill|Inatsuhiko Shrine|Q119929655|qid=Q119929655}} (Ubocho, Ikeda City) is also known as another shrine that enshrines Inatsuhiko. k|Round tomb|Q11394747}}There is a theory that the shrine that is enshrined on top of the shrine is the original Shikinai shrine "Tamenatsuhiko Shrine", but the details are not clear{{Sfn|Minoh City History Main volume Volume 1|1964|pp=41-53}}{{Sfn|Tamenatsuhiko Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}.

=== History ===
Founding date is unknown. As mentioned above, it is thought that the shrine began with a ritual by a powerful clan living in the Ina region. It is known that a {{ill|Dōtaku|Q2312868|qid=Q2312868}} (Nyoidani Dotaku) was excavated in Nyoidani, Minoh City, to the west of the precincts, and there is a theory that suggests that it is related to the Fuchigen of Tamenatsuhiko Shrine {{Sfn|Tamenatsuhiko Shrine (Gods)|2000}}.

{{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Extended}}5 years ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}) "{{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448}}" {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shinmyocho}} is {{ill|Settsu Province|ca|Província de Settsu|cs|Provincie Seccu|de|Provinz Settsu|eo|Provinco Seccu|es|Provincia de Settsu|fa|ولایت ستسو|fr|Province de Settsu|gl|Provincia de Settsu|hak|Settsu-koet|id|Provinsi Settsu|it|Settsu (provincia)|ja|摂津国|ko|셋쓰국|lt|Seccu žemė|nl|Settsu (provincie)|pt|Província de Settsu|ru|Сэтцу (провинция)|simple|Settsu Province|sk|Seccu (provincia)|sr|Провинција Сецу|tr|Settsu (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Сеццу|zh|攝津國|zh_min_nan|Settu-kok|zh_yue|攝津國|qid=Q864163}}{{ill|Teshima district|Q11633558|qid=Q11633558|lt=Toshima District}} is described as ``Tamenatuhiko Shrine 2nd Shrine'', and the 2nd shrine is listed in {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} {{Sfn|Tamenatuhiko Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}. Among the place names that appear in ``{{ill|Wamyō Ruijushō|Q2702542|qid=Q2702542|lt=Japanese Namesho}}'' from the middle of the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}, this place is compared to Toshima District Ekiyago {{Sfn|Tamenatsuhiko Shrine (Gods)|2000}}.

The {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}} festival is described in ``{{ill|Settsu Meisho Zue|ja|摂津名所図会|qid=Q11498549}}'' and other documents {{Sfn|Tamenatsuhiko Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}.After {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, in {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}}5 ({{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}}), {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern company rank system}} {jalink|Murasha|Q134917284}}, and was designated as a Shinto food shrine in February of 1907 ({{ill|1907|Q2048|qid=Q2048}}). On June 14, 1907, in addition to the aforementioned Omiya Shrine, ten other shrines from the former {{ill|Kayano|Q11620526|qid=Q11620526|lt=Kayano Village}} were enshrined together.

=== Historical evidence ===
[[File:Inadera-haiji1.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|{{ill|Inadera haiji ato|Q11571866|qid=Q11571866}}({{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|Q130290|qid=Q130290}}{{ill|Amagasaki|Q213318|qid=Q213318}})}}{{small|While the Ina-dera Temple area is considered to be the center of the Ina region, Tamenatsuhiko Shrine is located at the eastern end of the Ina region. }}]]
There are various theories regarding the Hosai clan of Tamenatsuhiko Shrine. As a factor for considering specific Hosai clans, it is known that in ``{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|Q1045362|qid=Q1045362}}'' the following clans whose headquarters are in Settsu Province are described.
:* Settsu Province Kobetsu Tamena Masato - After the {{ill|Emperor Senka|Q329728|qid=Q329728}} prince's Flame King.
:* Lord Kawahara of Settsu Province - Same ancestor of Masato Tamena. After the Prince of Fire. During the reign of Emperor Tenji, he was given the surname of Kawahara.
:* Sakyojinbetsu Inabezo - After {{ill|Ikagashiko-o|fr|Ikagashikoo|ja|伊香色雄|qid=Q55536799|lt=Ikagairoo no Mikoto}}.
:* Settsu Province Morobaku Tamenabushi - Originated from Nakatsunabite from Baekje Province.
:* Undetermined miscellaneous name in Settsu Province Tamenabushi - After Kinren, the 6th grandson of Ikagashiki no Mikoto.Among the above, Masato Tamena (Tamena clan) mentioned at the beginning is a clan that can be seen in {{ill|Rikkokushi|Q1151168|qid=Q1151168|lt=Kokushi}}, and {{ill|Ban Nobutomo|Q4346747|qid=Q4346747}} is a clan mentioned in our company's festival in "{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō Dodai|Q11588823|qid=Q11588823}}". There is a theory that the deity is compared to the ancestral deity of the Tamanatsuhiko people, and in ``{{ill|Tokusen Jinmyōchō|ja|特選神名牒|qid=Q11571092}}'' there is also a theory that the enshrined deity is compared to Prince Kamishiha, the son of Emperor Senka (the ancestor of the Prince Eba, Prince Iina/Kimi Iina).{{Sfn|Tamenatsuhiko Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}.On the other hand, the ancient center of the Ina region (and {{ill|Korean clans|Q846706|qid=Q846706|lt=Honkanchi}} of the Tamena and Kawahara clans) was Kawabe District (Kawabe District) Tamenago (present-day {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|Q130290|qid=Q130290}}{{ill|Amagasaki|Q213318|qid=Q213318}} is believed to be {{Sfn|Tamena clan (Dictionary of Ancient Clan Names)|2010}}, and Tamenatuhiko Shrine is named after "Ina". Although it is a shrine, it is located at the eastern end of the Ina region (Ekiiego, Toshima District), so the theory that the Hosai clan is the Tamena clan is strongly denied {{Sfn|Minoh City History Main volume Volume 1 | 1964 | pp=41-53}}{{Sfn|Tenatsuhiko Shrine Niza (Shikinai Shrine) | 1977}}{{Sfn|Tamenatsuhiko Shrine (Gods) | 2000}}.為奈氏以外の説としては、上記の{{ill|Mononobe clan|Q1755836|qid=Q1755836}}系・渡来系の猪名部氏（為奈部氏）と想定する説や、『摂陽群談』で大宮神社の祭祀にSince the Tokihara clan ({{ill|Hata clan|Q987290|qid=Q987290}} branch clan) is involved, there is a theory that it is assumed to be the Hata clan {{Sfn|Tamenatsuhiko Shrine (Gods)|2000}}.In addition, "{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ar|نيهون شوكي|as|নিহন শ্ব'কি|az|Nihon şoki|bcl|Nihon Shoki|bg|Нихоншоки|ca|Nihon Shoki|cs|Nihonšoki|de|Nihonshoki|el|Νιχόν Σόκι|eo|Nihon Ŝoki|es|Nihonshoki|eu|Nihon Shoki|fa|نیهون شوکی|fi|Nihonshoki|fr|Nihon shoki|gl|Nihon Shoki|he|ניהון שוקי|hi|निहोन शोकी|hr|Nihon Shoki|hu|Nihonsoki|id|Nihon Shoki|it|Nihon shoki|ja|日本書紀|jv|Nihon Shoki|ko|일본서기|la|Nihon Shoki|mk|Нихон шоки|ms|Nihon Shoki|my|နိဟွန်းရှောခိ|nl|Nihon Shoki|no|Nihonshoki|oc|Nihon shoki|pl|Nihon-shoki|pt|Nihon Shoki|rsk|Нихон Шоки|ru|Нихон сёки|sco|Nihon Shoki|sh|Nihon Shoki|simple|Nihon Shoki|sl|Nihon Šoki|sq|Nihon Shoki|sr|Нихон шоки|sv|Nihonshoki|ta|நிஹான் ஷோகி|th|นิฮงโชกิ|tl|Nihon Shoki|tr|Nihon Shoki|uk|Ніхон Сьокі|uz|Nihon shoki|vi|Nhật Bản thư kỷ|zh|日本書紀|zh_min_nan|Ji̍t-pún Su-kì|zh_yue|日本書紀|qid=Q813935}}" states that "{{ill|local government in classical Japan|Q11410912|qid=Q11410912|lt=Agatha}}" jalink|Ina Prefecture|Q11571881}}", there is also a theory that the Hosai clan of our company served as the head of Ina Prefecture.{{Sfn|History of Minoh City Main volume Volume 1 | 1964 | pp=41-53}}{{Sfn|Ninatsuhiko Shrine Niza (Shikiuchi Shrine) | 1977}}.
